core_obligations: Set up the inverse map (proof lines 1432-1436): for a torsor trivial along each member of the covering the author chooses a section over each member, using the triviality criterion.

Produce the cocycle (proof lines 1436-1441): on the fibre products over the covering the chosen sections differ by a unique section of the sheaf, and those sections form a Cech cocycle whose class is independent of the choices.

Read off the statement (proof lines 1442-1444): the inverse map sends the isomorphism class of the torsor to the class of that cocycle, and the author omits only the verification that it is an inverse, which is a routine tail.
proof_roadmap: Choose sections of the torsor over the members of the covering.
Form the Cech cocycle measuring their disagreement on the fibre products.
Observe that its class is well defined and gives the inverse map of the statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that Cech H-1 of a covering injects into the first cohomology group and identifies it with the isomorphism classes of torsors trivial along the covering (statement lines 1415-1429). The proof constructs the inverse map explicitly: it chooses a section of the torsor over each member of the covering using the triviality criterion (proof lines 1432-1436), forms the Cech cocycle measuring the disagreement of those sections on the fibre products, checks that its class is well defined (proof lines 1436-1441), and records that the map so defined is the required inverse (proof lines 1442-1444). The author omits only the verification that the construction is an inverse, a routine tail which is retained verbatim inside the counted span. The claim is H2: one explicit construction.
